name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run a controlled A/B test on the top-used prompt by splitting traffic 50/50 between the current version and a stripped-down, faster version. The trade-off is accepting a brief drop in output quality for measurable speed gains. If the faster version holds within 5% of the original’s quality metrics, we auto-apply it across the board—this proves the routing system can improve without sacrificing user trust.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just that a stripped-down prompt might hurt performance—it’s that we’re assuming we can measure “quality” accurately enough to detect a 5% drop. A better alternative is to run a shadow test first: mirror all traffic to both versions without exposing users, then compare outputs offline before risking live splits. Settle it by defining the quality metric upfront—if the faster version fails to meet the original’s baseline in the shadow test, we scrap the idea before touching live traffic.
